definition: to crush something into very small pieces or powder

collocations.example: She likes to grind coffee beans every morning.
The machine can grind the grain into fine powder.

definition: a person who is legally responsible for the care of another, especially a child

collocations.example: Her grandmother became her legal guardian after the accident.
The court named an aunt as the child's guardian.

definition: a large area of sea that is partly enclosed by land

collocations.example: Many oil refineries line the Gulf coast of Texas.
Oil tankers cross the Persian Gulf every single day.

definition: the tube in the body through which food passes during digestion

collocations.example: Healthy gut bacteria help the body digest food properly.
Scientists study how the human gut absorbs nutrients.

definition: the natural environment where a particular animal or plant normally lives

collocations.example: The panda's natural habitat is the bamboo forest.
Habitat destruction threatens many rare species with extinction.

definition: a tool with a heavy metal head used for hitting nails

collocations.example: He pulled the bent nail out with a claw hammer.
She swung the hammer hard and drove the nail in.

definition: something that makes it harder for someone to succeed or do something

collocations.example: He worked hard to overcome his physical handicap.
Not speaking the language was a serious handicap abroad.

definition: having an attractive, good-looking appearance, especially a man

collocations.example: He grew into a tall, handsome young man.
The hero was ruggedly handsome and quietly confident.

definition: to annoy or trouble someone repeatedly, often in a threatening way

collocations.example: Managers must not harass workers over minor mistakes.
The debt collectors constantly harass her by phone.

definition: the physical machines and equipment that make up a computer system

collocations.example: The company upgraded all its computer hardware last year.
The price includes both the hardware and the software.

definition: a situation in which people live or work together peacefully

collocations.example: The two communities have learned to live in harmony.
The policy aims to promote social harmony and trust.

definition: the activity of gathering crops, or the crops that are gathered

collocations.example: Plenty of rain gave the farmers a good harvest.
The whole village helps out at harvest time.

definition: the act of doing something quickly, often too quickly

collocations.example: The letter had clearly been written in haste.
We must make haste or we will miss the train.

definition: to break out of an egg, or to cause an egg to break open

collocations.example: The hen will hatch her eggs in about three weeks.
The baby chicks finally hatched out early this morning.

definition: to pull something heavy with a lot of effort

collocations.example: They used a rope to haul up the heavy crate.
The fishermen slowly hauled in the loaded net.

definition: to keep causing worry or trouble to someone over time

collocations.example: His lie would later come back to haunt him.
The accident continued to haunt her dreams for years.

definition: a person who will legally receive money, property, or a title when someone dies

collocations.example: The young prince is the heir to the throne.
He claims to be the rightful heir to the estate.

definition: an aircraft that flies using large rotating blades on top

collocations.example: A rescue helicopter lifted them from the sinking boat.
They were eventually rescued by helicopter.

definition: a hard hat that protects the head from injury

collocations.example: All workers must wear a safety helmet on site.
A man in a crash helmet was mounting a motorcycle.

definition: a plant used to add flavor to food or to make medicine

collocations.example: She flavored the soup with fresh herbs from the garden.
This medicinal herb is sold in most health shops.

definition: a large group of animals of one kind that live together

collocations.example: A herd of cattle blocked the narrow country road.
With no predators, the whole herd increased rapidly.

definition: a system in which people or things are ranked by importance or level

collocations.example: She slowly rose through the company's social hierarchy.
The firm has a rigid hierarchy of managers and staff.

definition: having an empty space inside rather than being solid

collocations.example: The owl nested inside a hollow tree by the river.
Water flows quickly through the narrow hollow tube.

definition: the metal cover over the engine of a car (American English)

collocations.example: The mechanic looked under the hood of the car.
Steam poured out when he opened the hood.

definition: to move by making short jumps, especially on one foot

collocations.example: The child hopped over the puddle on the path.
The rabbit hopped around the garden looking for food.

definition: the line far away where the sky seems to meet the land or sea

collocations.example: A ship slowly appeared on the horizon.
The sun sank below the horizon at dusk.

definition: flat and level, going from side to side rather than up and down

collocations.example: The board consists of vertical and horizontal lines.
Dust had settled on every horizontal surface in the room.

definition: a chemical in the body that controls how cells and organs work

collocations.example: Children need growth hormone to develop properly.
Oestrogen is an important female sex hormone.

definition: a device on a vehicle that makes a loud warning sound

collocations.example: She pressed the car horn to warn the cyclist.
The driver sounded the horn as the child ran out.

definition: a person held prisoner until certain demands are met

collocations.example: The robbers took two bank clerks hostage.
Somebody is holding your wife hostage.

definition: the act of putting your arms around someone to show affection

collocations.example: She gave her mother a big hug.
He greeted his old friend with a warm bear hug.

definition: not proud; having a modest view of your own importance

collocations.example: He always makes much of his humble origins.
Despite his fame, he has remained remarkably humble.

definition: to make someone feel ashamed or foolish, especially in front of others

collocations.example: She felt he had publicly humiliated her at the meeting.
I didn't want to humiliate her in front of her colleagues.

definition: a violent storm with very strong winds, especially in the Atlantic

collocations.example: A powerful hurricane hit the coast overnight.
The eye of the hurricane passed just south of Miami.

definition: a small, simple building, often made of wood or mud

collocations.example: They spent the night in a small mountain hut.
The farmer stored his tools in a wooden hut.

definition: something made by combining two different things or types

collocations.example: Hybrid cars use both petrol and electric power.
A mule is a hybrid of a horse and a donkey.

definition: a light, colorless gas that is the simplest chemical element

collocations.example: Hydrogen and oxygen combine to form water.
The country secretly tested a powerful hydrogen bomb.

definition: exactly the same in every detail

collocations.example: The identical twins were impossible to tell apart.
Her dress is almost identical to mine.

definition: relating to a set of political or social beliefs

collocations.example: Deep ideological differences split the political party.
Physical and ideological barriers came down across Europe.

definition: not working or being used; not active

collocations.example: Now the expensive machine is lying idle.
Hundreds of workers stood idle during the strike.

definition: to shine light on something so it can be seen

collocations.example: Candles illuminated the room with a soft glow.
The stage was brightly illuminated for the evening show.

definition: a false idea or belief, or something that seems real but is not

collocations.example: The drawing is a clever optical illusion.
Mirrors create an illusion of space in small rooms.

definition: to copy the way someone or something looks, sounds, or behaves

collocations.example: Children often imitate the adults around them.
The clever bird can imitate the sound of a phone.

definition: extremely large in size or degree

collocations.example: The manager was under immense pressure to succeed.
Visitors are amazed by the immense size of the cathedral.

definition: to make something weaker or less effective

collocations.example: Even one drink can impair your judgment while driving.
The injury seriously impaired his ability to walk.

definition: easily annoyed by having to wait or by delays

collocations.example: He grew impatient with the slow service.
She was clearly impatient to leave the party early.

definition: suggested or understood without being directly stated

collocations.example: There was an implicit assumption that she would pay.
A clear warning was implicit in his quiet tone.

definition: a sudden strong wish to do something without thinking

collocations.example: He bought the car on impulse.
I had to resist the impulse to laugh out loud.

definition: how often something, especially a problem or disease, happens

collocations.example: The region has a high incidence of lung cancer.
Better hygiene lowered the incidence of disease sharply.

definition: a slope, or a surface that rises or falls

collocations.example: The truck struggled up the steep incline slowly.
The path rose on a gentle incline toward the house.

definition: the act of including someone or something, or being included

collocations.example: The charity promotes social inclusion for disabled people.
The inclusion of charts made the report much clearer.

definition: not interested in or concerned about something

collocations.example: He seemed completely indifferent to their suffering.
Voters cannot remain indifferent to such important issues.

definition: originating naturally in a particular place; native

collocations.example: The indigenous people have lived here for centuries.
Several indigenous species are found only on this island.

definition: not happening in a direct or straight way

collocations.example: He took an indirect route back home.
The building collapsed as an indirect result of the flood.

definition: to persuade or cause someone to do something

collocations.example: Nothing could induce him to change his mind.
The adverts are designed to induce customers to buy.

definition: to allow yourself to enjoy something pleasant, especially a treat

collocations.example: Only rarely will she indulge in a glass of wine.
On holiday she loves to indulge herself with spa treatments.

definition: to form an opinion or conclusion from available information

collocations.example: What can we infer from the passage about the author?
We can safely infer that sales will keep rising.

definition: without any limit or end; extremely great

collocations.example: Nature offers an almost infinite variety of forms.
Teaching young children requires almost infinite patience.

definition: to make strong feelings, especially anger, even stronger

collocations.example: His careless comments only inflamed the situation further.
The speech inflamed passions on both sides of the debate.

definition: relaxed and friendly; not official or formal

collocations.example: We settled the matter at an informal meeting.
Interviews often feel easier in an informal setting.

definition: the basic systems and structures a country needs to work, such as roads

collocations.example: The city invested heavily in its transport infrastructure.
Simple improvements to infrastructure can reduce the spread of disease.

definition: existing as a natural and permanent part of something

collocations.example: Every investment carries a certain inherent risk.
Individuality is an inherent part of her character.

definition: to prevent or slow down a process or action

collocations.example: A lack of sunlight can inhibit plant growth.
Too much authority can inhibit innovation at work.

definition: a colored liquid used for writing or printing

collocations.example: The printer needs a new black ink cartridge.
The factory produces printing ink for local newspapers.

definition: a small hotel or pub, especially in the countryside

collocations.example: We spent the night at a cosy country inn.
Travelers used to stay at an inn along the road.

definition: introducing or using new ideas and methods

collocations.example: The phone's innovative design won several major awards.
Her innovative approach to teaching impressed the whole school.

definition: a small creature with six legs and usually wings

collocations.example: She scratched at the insect bites on her arm.
Apply insect repellent before walking in the forest.

definition: to cover something to stop heat, sound, or electricity escaping

collocations.example: People should insulate their homes to conserve energy.
Thick walls insulate the building against the winter cold.

definition: a rude or offensive remark or action

collocations.example: Their behavior was an insult to the whole team.
The angry crowd began to hurl insults at him.

definition: complete and not damaged

collocations.example: Most of the house remains intact after two hundred years.
Few of the old buildings survived the war intact.

definition: forming a necessary and essential part of something

collocations.example: Teamwork is an integral part of the job.
Good lighting is integral to the room's design.

definition: the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles

collocations.example: Her personal integrity was never once in doubt.
I have always regarded him as a man of integrity.

definition: able to learn, understand, and think quickly and well

collocations.example: She is a highly intelligent and curious student.
The dolphin is a very intelligent animal.

definition: the way a user interacts with a computer program or device

collocations.example: The app has a simple, friendly user interface.
The system uses an impressive graphical interface.

definition: temporary and intended to be used until something permanent is ready

collocations.example: An interim government ruled until the next election.
The committee published an interim report last week.

definition: a period of time between two events or actions

collocations.example: Buses leave at regular intervals throughout the day.
The process is repeated after a short interval.

definition: to frighten someone, especially to make them do what you want

collocations.example: The gang tried to intimidate witnesses before the trial.
She is confident and not easily intimidated by anyone.

definition: secret planning to do something, often harmful or dishonest

collocations.example: The palace was full of political intrigue and rumor.
He found himself caught in a web of intrigue.

definition: to enter a country or area with an army to take control

collocations.example: The army prepared to invade the neighboring country.
Troops moved quickly to invade and occupy the city.

definition: to use a law, rule, or principle as a reason for action

collocations.example: The lawyer chose to invoke an older trade law.
They invoked the principle of free speech in court.

definition: to make someone feel annoyed or impatient

collocations.example: His constant jokes began to irritate some people.
She was tired and easily irritated by small things.

definition: a glass or clay container with a wide opening and a lid

collocations.example: She kept the homemade honey in a glass jar.
He opened a fresh jar of strawberry jam.

definition: a type of music with strong rhythm and improvisation

collocations.example: He put some jazz music on the stereo.
A lively jazz band played at the wedding.

definition: a sudden, quick, sharp movement

collocations.example: The train stopped with a sudden jerk.
He pulled the cord free with a sharp jerk.

definition: decorative items worn on the body, such as rings and necklaces

collocations.example: She has some lovely pieces of jewelry.
The market sells cheap costume jewelry to tourists.

definition: relating to courts of law or judges

collocations.example: Bias against women permeates the whole judicial system.
The case is now subject to judicial review.

definition: a thick tropical forest with many plants and trees

collocations.example: The explorers hacked through the dense jungle for days.
The rare bird lives deep in the jungle.

definition: the official power to make legal decisions, or the area it covers

collocations.example: The crime falls under a different legal jurisdiction.
This case falls outside my jurisdiction.

definition: relating to young people who are not yet adults

collocations.example: Juvenile crime is increasing at a terrifying rate.
She was sent to the juvenile court instead of prison.

definition: the set of keys used to type on a computer or typewriter

collocations.example: Learn this keyboard shortcut to save yourself time.
Her fingers moved quickly as she typed on the keyboard.

definition: to take someone away illegally and hold them by force

collocations.example: The gang planned to kidnap a wealthy businessman's child.
Police foiled an attempt to kidnap the diplomat.

definition: a unit of weight equal to one thousand grams

collocations.example: We bought a kilogram of fresh lemons.
The apples are sold at two dollars per kilogram.

definition: a person's family and relatives

collocations.example: The police have notified the next of kin.
He left his home, his kith and kin behind.

definition: a set of tools or equipment used for a particular purpose

collocations.example: Keep a well-stocked first aid kit for emergencies.
He carries a small tool kit in his van.

definition: to go down or stay on your knees

collocations.example: She knelt down to tie her child's shoe.
The knights would kneel before the king.

definition: a join made by tying together pieces of string or rope

collocations.example: She tied a knot in the cherry stem.
His clumsy fingers could not untie the knot.

definition: a delicate decorative fabric made with patterns of holes

collocations.example: She wore a gown beautifully trimmed with white lace.
Fine lace curtains hung across the old windows.

definition: a piece of equipment with steps used for climbing up and down

collocations.example: He had to climb a ladder to fix the roof.
She was halfway up the ladder when it wobbled.
